name: August Jackson
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember a letter arriving on the wrong continent.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know August by a small Saturday habit. August pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I fold the cards into boats. My granddaughter can open them only by reading flags.
appearance: August has short copper curls, a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, an olive canvas jacket. It usually goes with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. When somebody else has the floor, August takes off the watch before a long conversation.
personality: August keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. August wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To teach the grandchild to unfold the flagged card.
family: Patricia Ramos is August’s younger relative by marriage. August offers the first invitation. Patricia gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The late crossing*, Patricia says, “I used to get lifts from my boss until I felt I couldn't refuse overtime.”
connections: Lee Murphy. A folded boat reaches one grandchild while a dance-hall print finds an old partner.

reactions.response: August checks whether the families want their messages used outside the envelopes.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: August asks them privately what can be shared about the delay and respects the answer.
